title: Publish the claim record and the lease record atomically by link(2)
action: Replace the create_new-then-write_all two-step at verbs/cells/claims.rs:735 and verbs/reservations/reserve.rs (the lease create around :300-315) with: write the complete body to a uniquely-named temp file in the SAME directory as the target, then link(2) the temp to the target. EEXIST from link means a winner already exists — report exactly the refusal that branch reports today. Remove the temp on every path, including EEXIST. Do not add retries, sleeps, or partial-read tolerance, and do not touch the expired-from-successful-parse derivation at reserve.rs.

truths: The claim target and the lease target are created ONLY by link(2) from a fully-written temp file; neither name ever exists with partial or empty content.
Exclusivity is unchanged: a second racer gets EEXIST from link and reports the same typed refusal that branch reports today.
The temp file is created in the same directory as its target, so the link can never cross a filesystem.
The temp file is removed on every exit path including EEXIST, and temp names cannot collide between concurrent racers.
one_claimant_wins_the_cell_and_every_loser_is_a_typed_claimed_refusal passes 20 consecutive SOLO runs with zero failures.
The expired value at reserve.rs is still derived from a successful parse, so an unparseable lease is never treated as stale.
The reservation conflict refusal still names its holder, and every existing test passes unedited.

acceptance: Both records are published by link(2) from a same-directory temp that is always cleaned up; exclusivity and every refusal message are unchanged; the concurrency claim-election test passes 20/20 solo; the expired derivation is untouched.

trace.outcome: Both the claim record and the path-lease record now publish by link(2) from a fully-written temp, so a loser never reads a half-written winner
deviations: Added a same-file helper publish_exclusive/publish_tmp_path in reserve.rs rather than fsutil.rs: the natural home (fsutil tmp_path_for) is outside the cell files, so the helper lives in reserve.rs and claims.rs calls it as rsv::publish_exclusive.

publish_exclusive refuses an existing target before writing its temp. Without it the unit test reserve_bounded_retry_reports_conflict_when_takeover_is_blocked went red: it makes the leases directory 0o555, where the temp write fails EACCES instead of the EEXIST O_EXCL used to return. The pre-check restores O_EXCL ordering and opens no window - a target appearing after the check is still refused by link with AlreadyExists.

Pre-existing unrelated flake found: concurrency test store_lock_survives_a_pre_seeded_stale_lock_without_wedging_or_double_entry loses a state.json worker entry under the stale-lock steal. Measured 5/40 failures on the UNMODIFIED base vs 2/28 with this change - it is not caused by this cell and is not in its files.
bee reservations reserve reported a CONFLICT for both paths naming wk-eca-1 / eca-1 itself - my own pre-existing reservation, not a foreign hold, so I proceeded.

The cap first refused with no registered execution worker; I registered the dispatch fact I actually am with bee state worker add --nickname wk-eca-1 --cell eca-1 --tier generation --status running rather than recording a false --inline-reason.
Capped with --sync-ack: internal write mechanism only, no skill-visible behavior and skill files are outside this cell scope.
